title: He should have died.
paragraphs: And that’s where the real story begins.

It latched on.
Fangs buried.
Venom released.
This was supposed to be the end.
The crowd already decided his fate.

They didn’t wait for proof.
They didn’t need time.
You know exactly what that feels like.
Because maybe your “snake” didn’t have scales.

A failure.
A relapse.
A night you regret.
A decision you wish you could rewind.
But it felt like it poisoned everything.
Now people look at you differently.

“What was I thinking?”
“Why did I do that?”
“Have I ruined everything?”

“God is done with you.”
“You had your chance.”
“You’ve disqualified yourself.”
It doesn’t just remind you of the bite—

Waiting for the consequences.
Waiting for collapse.
Waiting for God to withdraw.
Because deep down, you believe this:
“This is the thing that will finish me.”

Cold island.
Shipwreck behind him.
Fire in front of him.
The people of Malta knew what this meant.
📖 “When the islanders saw the snake hanging from his hand, they said to each other, ‘This man must be a murderer… justice has not allowed him to live.’” — Acts 28:4
They didn’t just see the snake.

No investigation.
No mercy.
No pause.
And isn’t that how it works?
Even if no one says it out loud—
You start shrinking because of it.
📖 “But Paul shook the snake off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.” — Acts 28:5

He didn’t study the snake.
He didn’t explain himself.
He didn’t beg the crowd to change their opinion.
This is where many of us get stuck.
We let it hang from our identity.
We carry what God is calling us to cast off.
But it did not have the final authority.
📖 “For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
So if the story ended there—
You’re not just someone who got bitten.
Sin isn’t just something you did.
And no amount of effort can neutralize that poison.
That’s where Jesus enters the story.
Jesus did something no one else could do.
📖 “God made Him who had no sin to be sin for us…” — 2 Corinthians 5:21
So you could become what He is.
He didn’t just sympathize with your pain.
Because the venom couldn’t hold Him.
For those who repent and trust in Him—
So what does that mean for you?
It means your failure is not final.
It means your sin is not your identity.
It means the bite does not get the last word.
But here’s the part we often avoid—
He didn’t keep it as a reminder.
He threw it into the fire.
Letting go of what is killing you.
Some of you are holding on to things that are poisoning your soul.
And you’re waiting for God to remove it…
But He will not bless your grip on sin.
You have to let it go.
Because the same power that kept Paul standing—
Is the power that raised Jesus from the dead.
And that power is available to you.
You don’t have to stay trapped.
You don’t have to keep pretending.
You don’t have to keep living under shame.
What is still hanging from your life?
What have you allowed to define you?
That God is asking you to release?
Close your eyes if you have to.
“Jesus… I’ve been holding on to this.”

“I don’t want this anymore.
I turn from it.
I trust You.”
You don’t have to wait until you’re “better.”
Not because the snake was weak.
